course.title: Atomic – Cambridge Lower Secondary Mathematics — Stage 9

unit.title: Probability
unit.blurb: Mutually exclusive events, independent events, combined events with sample spaces and tree diagrams, and chance experiments.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Understand mutually exclusive events and use the fact that their probabilities add to 1 when they cover all outcomes.

O2.t: Understand independent events and multiply their probabilities.

O3.t: Find probabilities of combined events using sample-space diagrams, lists and tree diagrams.

O4.t: Carry out chance experiments, find relative frequency and compare it with theoretical probability.

p: Events are **mutually exclusive** if they **cannot happen at the same time**: rolling a 2 and rolling a 5 on one dice.
For mutually exclusive events, **P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B)**. If the events cover every outcome, their probabilities **add up to 1**, so **P(not A) = 1 − P(A)**.

p: A **sample-space diagram** shows every outcome of two events. For two dice there are 6 × 6 = **36** equally likely outcomes.
Count the outcomes you want and divide by the total.
On a **tree diagram**, multiply **along** the branches, then **add** the end results you want.
Without replacement, the second-stage probabilities change because there is one fewer item.

p: **Relative frequency = number of times the event happened ÷ number of trials.** It is an estimate of the probability.
The **more trials**, the more reliable the estimate. If the relative frequency is far from the theoretical probability after many trials, the object may be **biased**.

lesson.q: A spinner landed on blue 42 times in 120 spins. Estimate how many blues in 500 spins.

p: Ten flips giving 7 heads does not prove a coin is biased – the sample is too small. Use many trials before deciding.
